claims.claim: USA Used Canon EOS Rebel T1i with 18-55mm Lens
claims.evidence: Brand, model badge, and lens focal markings visible in photo 0 and photo 1; 'USA Used' origin itself cannot be confirmed from photos alone.

claims.claim: working perfectly ok with no fault
claims.evidence: No photo shows the screen powered on, a test shot, shutter firing, or lens autofocus/zoom in action; photo 2 shows a dark/reflective screen that does not confirm it is on or functional.

risks.risk: LCD screen may be faulty or dead
risks.proof: A photo or clip of the screen powered on displaying a live view or menu

risks.risk: Sensor or lens may have fungus, dust, or scratches affecting image quality
risks.proof: Close-up photo through the lens against a light source, and a sample photo taken with the camera

risks.risk: Shutter mechanism wear or failure (shutter count unknown)
risks.proof: A clip of the shutter firing, or a screenshot of shutter count from EOS utility/software
risks.if_unproven: priced as shutter condition unknown/high wear

risks.risk: Battery, charger, and memory card may not be included
risks.proof: Photo of battery, charger, and card included in the sale
risks.if_unproven: priced as body and lens only, no accessories

risks.risk: Body may have drop damage, dents, or internal issues not visible from these angles
risks.proof: Additional photos from top, bottom, and side angles, plus of the battery/card compartment
risks.if_unproven: priced as cosmetic condition unknown beyond shown angles

proof_requests: Photo or short video of the camera powered on with the LCD screen showing a live image or menu
A sample photo taken with the camera to confirm sensor and lens image quality
Photo of the battery compartment and memory card slot, and any included battery/charger
Clip of the shutter firing or a shutter-count screenshot
Full body photos from top, bottom, and both sides to check for dents or drop damage
response.reason: The camera and lens are clearly identified by brand and model from the photos, but the 'working perfectly' claim is unverifiable since no power-on, test shot, or shutter action is shown, so it must be priced at worst case as not confirmed working.
